extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewers assigned NeurIPS 2020 submissions, covering responsibilities, review content, scoring, confidentiality, conflicts, discussion, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect deadlines and timely communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Please respect deadlines and respond to emails as promptly as possible!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is crucial that we are able to reach you in a timely manner. We will send most emails from CMT (email@msr-cmt.org). Such emails are sometimes marked as spam—check spam folder and whitelist the CMT email address. If you change your email address, update CMT. Keep domain conflicts in CMT up to date; these are important for preventing conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check conflicts of interest immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as reviewers are notified of papers to review, reviewers are expected to log in to CMT to check for conflicts and to check that papers fall within the area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not comfortable reviewing a paper, fill out a note in CMT and communicate to your AC immediately so an alternate qualified reviewer can be found in time. Read what constitutes conflict of interest for NeurIPS 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer profile for good matching
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS uses TPMS and OpenReview to assign submissions; please log into TPMS and OpenReview to make sure your profile is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a stale profile causes poor assignments that may be outside your area of expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by NeurIPS code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants must agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must accord with the code of conduct. Avoid discriminatory language or implications. Example: instead of saying 'proof-read by a native English speaker' use neutral language like 'proof-read for English style and grammar issues.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities (scope of work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are responsible for reviewing submissions, reading author responses, discussing submissions and author responses with other reviewers and area chairs, and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reviewer will be assigned around 4–6 submissions unless a smaller quota specified. The process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs; reviewer identities are visible to other reviewers, ACs and SACs. After decisions, reviews and meta-reviews become public (identities remain anonymous). Engage actively in the discussion phase for assigned submissions, even if not prompted by the AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep papers assigned to you in absolute confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas and results from submissions in your own work until they become publicly available. Do not discuss or distribute submissions or their ideas without prior approval from the program chairs. Do not talk to other reviewers/ACs/SACs about submissions assigned to you without prior AC approval; this also applies to your own submissions or submissions with which you have a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs; authors are responsible for anonymizing their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the corresponding AC. Under no circumstances should you attempt to find out authors' identities (e.g., by searching Google or arXiv). If you accidentally learn identities, do not divulge them. Do not let authors' identities influence your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material in PDF or ZIP format; your responsibility is to read and review the submission itself; looking at supplementary material is at your discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NeurIPS submissions are short, so you may wish to look at supplementary material before criticizing a submission for insufficient details, proofs, or experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety when executing submitted code or clicking links
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities; be cautious if you plan to run supplementary source code or follow links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run code only in a secure environment (recommended: inside a Docker container, a VM image, or on a network-isolated cloud instance). Be cautious with external web links as they may contain vulnerabilities or log visitor IP addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CMT for all review submissions and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews must be submitted via the NeurIPS 2020 CMT site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may revise reviews as often as necessary. Never reply directly to emails sent by CMT; instead, use the 'email meta-reviewer' and 'email senior meta-reviewer' links in CMT. If you are both an author and reviewer, use the same email address for both roles in CMT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages in the NeurIPS 'submission' style; additional pages allowed only for broader impact and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file. If assigned submissions violate style (e.g., decreasing margins or font size) or page limits, notify the AC immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and report dual submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted/published elsewhere (including other NeurIPS submissions) should be deemed dual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly may be dual submission. If you suspect a dual submission or need clarification, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write detailed, informative, constructive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your review as detailed and informative as possible; short, superficial reviews that venture uninformed opinions or guesses are worse than no review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review content is primary means for ACs/SACs to make decisions and for authors to understand outcomes. For rejected submissions, reviews should help authors improve; for accepted, help with camera-ready versions. Avoid dismissive or inappropriate language and give precise citations when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions (review form item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable to ACs/SACs/program chairs and helps detect misunderstandings. Contributions may be theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, bridge papers, or critical analyses. See Examples of Review Content for sample contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths (review form item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work; typical criteria include soundness of claims, significance and novelty, and relevance to NeurIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List strengths such as soundness of theory or experiments, significance/novelty relative to literature, likely uptake by community, and relevance to NeurIPS. Cite relevant prior work precisely when comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses (review form item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of this work along the same axes as strengths (soundness, significance, novelty, relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite; avoid vague subjective complaints. Remember you are evaluating scientific contribution, not personal interest in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness (review form item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims and methods are correct and whether the empirical methodology is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain any incorrectness in detail—incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection. Motivate criticisms thoroughly so authors can respond usefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (review form item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the clarity of exposition of the paper and give examples of parts needing revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete suggestions for improving clarity and organization; indicate missing equation numbers, unclear notation, or wrong appendix references as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work (review form item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether the submission clearly discusses how it differs from previous contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related work should not just list prior work but explain differences. Authors are excused for not knowing all non-refereed work (e.g., arXiv); papers appearing less than two months before submission are considered contemporaneous and authors aren't obligated to make detailed comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (review form item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether there are enough details to reproduce the major results of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not reproducible, list lack of reproducibility among weaknesses. Consider supplementary material if necessary to judge reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional feedback, suggestions, and questions (review form item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any additional comments, suggestions for improvement, or questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include requests for clarifications you expect authors to address in the author response (e.g., 'I would like to see results of experiment X').

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score with percentile guidance (review form item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an Overall Score reflecting your assessment of the submission's contributions, independent of assumed acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score mapping: 10=Top 5% accepted (groundbreaking); 9=Top 15% accepted; 8=Top 50% accepted; 7=good submission; 6=marginally above threshold; 5=marginally below; 4=okay but not good enough; 3=clear reject; 2=strong reject (surprised it was submitted); 1=trivial/wrong/already known. Do not adjust scores to match conference acceptance rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (review form item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how certain you are about your assessment on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5=absolutely certain (very familiar with related work), 4=confident but not absolute, 3=fairly confident (some parts not carefully checked), 2=willing to defend but likely gaps, 1=educated guess (not in area or hard-to-understand submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact adequacy (review form item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the authors have adequately addressed the broader impact of their work, including potential negative ethical and societal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to include a statement of potential broader impact discussing both positive and negative outcomes. Indicate Yes, No, or Partially and comment on adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging potential ethical concerns (review form item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the submission raises potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that create or reinforce unfair bias or that have primary purpose of harm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No. If Yes, explain briefly. This rating should be independent of your accept/reject rating. If AC shares concern, dedicated ethics reviewers may further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior reviewing/area chairing of same work (review form item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether you have previously reviewed or area chaired a version of this work for another archival venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes/No. This helps ACs/SACs contextualize your review; ACs may have access to a resubmission statement declaring prior rejections and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to NeurIPS code of conduct (review form item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that you agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided to full code of conduct; reviewers must agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to area chair (review form item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide confidential comments to the area chair that will not be shown to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for explicit comparisons to other submissions or blunt criticisms. Include sensitive information like discovered author identities if accidentally learned (but do not divulge identities publicly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and respond to author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read author responses and, if appropriate, respond or update their reviews after the author response period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore any author response. Update reviews to indicate you have read the response and whether you agree or disagree; be specific (not just 'opinion remains the same') and explain what was not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in the discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: After the author response phase, the AC will initiate discussion to encourage reviewers to come to a consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take discussion seriously, especially for borderline submissions or divergent reviewer assessments. Consider other reviewers' viewpoints and change your mind if appropriate; consensus is valuable but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation by area chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: 'exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', and 'failed to meet expectations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top ~8% reviewers (by these evaluations) receive free NeurIPS registrations; next ~30% have registrations reserved. Low-scoring reviewers may not be invited to review in future years—this encourages high-quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inappropriate contact or discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not talk to other reviewers, ACs, or SACs about submissions assigned to you without prior AC approval; also do not talk about your own submissions or submissions with which you have a conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary point of contact for discussions should be the corresponding AC for that submission. Be professional and polite in discussions; do not give in to undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of high-quality review content (contributions, quality, clarity, originality, significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples of what constitutes solid contributions and review comments across axes like contributions, technical quality, clarity, originality, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide provides multiple illustrative example quotes from past NeurIPS reviews addressing strong experimental validation, theoretical contributions, relating to prior work, pointing out technical issues, clarity problems, and significance. Use these as models for concrete, specific, and well-motivated review comments.
